newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end down, further fall seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end down, further fall seen.

text.p: Singapore's key share index shed more than one percent on Monday and dealers said further falls were expected this week.
"Realistically we're going lower, but because volumes are so low it's too hard to call whether the next low will be a technical or the key support level," one local dealer said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index dropped 25.92 points, or 1.23 percent, to 2,073.00 at Monday's close.
Dealers said a lack of positive news at home or in the United States, either corporate or economic, had left Singapore drifting down.
Losers swamped gainers 328 to 46 on a low volume of 117.1 million shares and dealers said selling was more on reaction than analysis.
"One slight sniff of a sell and the whole market falls," one dealer said.
Leading loser was DBS Bank's foreign share tranche, down Singapore $0.70 at S$16.80 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
In contrast, OCBC Bank stock rose S$0.35 gain to S$9.45 on news of a one-for-five bonus issue. The Malayan Bank 200 fund was the day's star performer, up S$0.60 at S$16.20.
